title: Frontend heads its two identification pages "Animal identification details" and "Additional animal details"; Design release 1 names them "Identification details" and "Additional details"

finding.frontend: Both pages in this section put the word "animal" in their own name. The identifier page is headed "Animal identification details" and the extra-facts page "Additional animal details" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:43 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/additional-details/copy/copy.en.js:2). Each name is used three times on its page — as the h1, as the last breadcrumb and as the browser tab title — so a trader reads it repeatedly. Nothing above either heading says which part of the notification they are in, which is why the heading is carrying the whole burden of orientation.
finding.prototype: Design release 1 names the same two pages "Identification details" and "Additional details", and puts the section above them instead: "About the consignment" over the first (app/views/animal-identification-details.html:3, with the caption and heading at :44-47) and "Commodity details" over the second (app/views/additional-animal-details.html:9, caption and heading at :37-38). The caption says what the pages are about, so the heading does not have to, and both names are shorter for it. The same name is used for the page name and the heading in both files.
finding.difference: Rename the two pages to "Identification details" and "Additional details". Each name lives once, in its feature's copy file, and feeds the heading, the breadcrumb and the tab title together, with a Welsh sibling to match. This is one string per page and nothing has to land first. It reads best alongside the section caption, which the service-wide slice owns and which is what makes the shorter names self-explanatory — but it does not depend on it, and the shorter names are the signed-off ones either way.
finding.falsifiedBy: A root view on the requirements side naming either page with the word "animal" in it. app/views/animal-identification-details.html sets pageName to "Identification details" and app/views/additional-animal-details.html sets it to "Additional details"; only the file names say animal.
finding.verification: Written and checked during verification of this slice, by a different agent than authored the slice's other findings. Ran the falsifier: grep for pageName across both Design release 1 root views returns "Identification details" and "Additional details" and neither contains the word animal. Read all four rendered DOMs: capture/html/frontend/fe-animal-identification.html:3 and :117 and capture/html/frontend/fe-additional-details.html:3 and :117 carry the long names in both the title and the h1, and capture/html/prototype/dr1-animal-identification-details.html:259 and capture/html/prototype/dr1-additional-animal-details.html:254 carry the short ones under their captions. Opened all four page shots to read the headings as rendered. Checked both requirements citations are root views under app/views and not release subfolders. No control is named: a page heading is not a control and would crop to the whole page, which is what a reader of this finding wants anyway.
finding.correction: Added by the verifier. The slice had no finding for either heading, and the certified-for-hint finding asserted that its hint was the only content difference on the additional details page, which sent a reader past this one. That sentence has been corrected in the same pass.

relatedTo.why: The shorter names work because Design release 1 puts the section caption above them; landing both together is what a trader actually sees.
